keyVerseText: And Iphedeiah, and Penuel, the sons of Shashak;
rootMeaning: The root of יִפְדְּיָה (Yiphdᵉyâh) is פָּדָה (pâdâh), which fundamentally means to redeem, ransom, or deliver. Combined with יָהּ (Jah), a shortened form of the divine name Jehovah, the name literally means 'Jehovah will redeem' or 'Jah will liberate.' This etymology enriches the understanding of the word by emphasizing divine intervention in the act of redemption, highlighting God's active role in rescuing and preserving His people beyond the general English sense of redemption.
usageInScripture: The word יִפְדְּיָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 8:25, where it is used as a proper name, Iphedeiah, identifying an Israelite descended from Benjamin and the family of Shashak. The sole translation recorded is 'And Iphedeiah,' indicating that the term functions as a personal name rather than a common noun. This limited usage underscores the significance of names in biblical genealogies, often conveying theological meaning embedded within the identity of the person.
theologicalSignificance: The name יִפְדְּיָה, meaning 'Jehovah will redeem,' carries profound theological weight, reminding believers of God's sovereign power to redeem and rescue His people. It reflects the covenantal faithfulness of God, who acts decisively to liberate and preserve His chosen ones. In the Christian faith, this name prefigures the ultimate redemption accomplished through Jesus Christ, who embodies God's redemptive work. Recognizing the divine element within personal names in Scripture enriches our appreciation of how God's character and promises are woven into the identity of His people.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 8:25, 'And Iphedeiah, and Penuel, the sons of Shashak,' the name Iphedeiah identifies a specific individual within the genealogical record. The meaning 'Jehovah will redeem' embedded in his name adds a layer of spiritual significance to this listing, suggesting that even amidst historical records, the theme of divine redemption is present. This reminds readers that every member of God's people is encompassed by His redeeming grace, reinforcing the continuity of God's saving work throughout Israel's history.
